questions.question: What are compound components? Show a Tabs example.
questions.title: Compound Components in React — Tabs Pattern Explained
questions.direct_answer:
What are compound components? Show a Tabs example.

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Parent manages shared state via Context; children communicate implicitly; ergonomic declarative API (Tabs, TabList, Tab, TabPanel).

**Classic weak answer:** Using prop-drilling between a Tabs parent and each Tab — Context cleanly expresses the implicit relationship.

**Senior finish:** Link to headless-UI libraries (Radix, Headless UI, Ark UI) that popularized this pattern.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **Compound Components in React — Tabs Pattern Explained** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What are compound components? Show a Tabs example.

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **Parent manages shared state via Context; children communicate implicitly; ergonomic declarative API (Tabs, TabList, Tab, TabPanel)**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Using prop-drilling between a Tabs parent and each Tab — Context cleanly expresses the implicit relationship**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Link to headless-UI libraries (Radix, Headless UI, Ark UI) that popularized this pattern**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** Parent manages shared state via Context; children communicate implicitly; ergonomic declarative API (Tabs, TabList, Tab, TabPanel)
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Mental model (flowchart)
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TB
    EVT[Event / state change] --> SCHED[Scheduler schedules update]
    SCHED --> DIFF[React reconciles virtual DOM]
    DIFF --> COMMIT[Commit DOM mutations]
    COMMIT --> FX[useLayoutEffect]
    COMMIT --> EF[useEffect after paint]
    subgraph Memo["Performance hooks"]
        MEMO[memo / useMemo / useCallback]
    end
    DIFF --> MEMO
```

| **Weak signal (avoid)** | Using prop-drilling between a Tabs parent and each Tab — Context cleanly expresses the implicit relationship |

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **using prop-drilling between a Tabs parent and each Tab — Context cleanly expresses the implicit relationship** and what you do instead.

sections.title: Key points (memorize this list)
sections.content:
- **Headline definition** in one sentence.
- **Mechanism:** Parent manages shared state via Context; children communicate implicitly; ergonomic declarative API (Tabs, TabList, Tab, TabPanel)
- **Pitfall:** Using prop-drilling between a Tabs parent and each Tab — Context cleanly expresses the implicit relationship
- **Differentiator:** Link to headless-UI libraries (Radix, Headless UI, Ark UI) that popularized this pattern
- **Proof:** DevTools / Network / Performance trace, test strategy, or metric.
- **Close:** decision rule + sensible follow-up question back to the interviewer.

sections.title: How to answer verbally (timed)
sections.content:
**Open (15–20 seconds):** Restate the question and give the one-sentence definition.

**Body (45–60 seconds):** Walk through **Parent manages shared state via Context; children communicate implicitly; ergonomic declarative API (Tabs, TabList, Tab, TabPanel)** as a story: what runs, what breaks, what you log/measure.

**Pitfall (15 seconds):** Call out **Using prop-drilling between a Tabs parent and each Tab — Context cleanly expresses the implicit relationship** — interviewers reward honesty about real bugs.

**Finish (15–20 seconds):** Add **Link to headless-UI libraries (Radix, Headless UI, Ark UI) that popularized this pattern**, then offer a trade-off question back (“do you optimize for TTFB or TTI here?”).
